sourceEnglishSpeaking: Tell the crew to tie off before roof access and ask them to point to the approved anchor.
candidateObjective: 屋根に上がる前の墜落防止用ハーネスの接続を明確に指示する。
candidateFocus: ～前に places the tie-off before roof access. ～ないでください prohibits an action; ～がなければ states the condition for not going up.

archivedForms.exampleJa: ハーネスなしでは誰も上がらないでください。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 全員が屋根に上がる前にハーネスを確認します。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Everyone checks their harness before going up.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 屋根に上がる前にハーネスをアンカーに接続します。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: We tie off the harness before going up on the roof.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 各自が承認されたアンカーを職長に見せます。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Each person shows the approved anchor to the foreman.

archivedForms.exampleJa: 墜落防止は各自が正しく使って初めて機能します。
archivedForms.exampleEnglish: Fall protection only works if each person uses it correctly.

archivedSpeaking.opening: 上がる前にハーネスを確認し、承認された屋根のアンカーに接続してください。アンカーを見せてください。
archivedSpeaking.goal: Tell the crew to tie off before roof access and ask them to point to the approved anchor.

internalSafetyReferences.use: Source review of anchorage and lower-level clearance; not learner-facing instruction
Review of total fall-distance and inspection factors; not an approved site plan

curriculumAdaptationNote: Preserve the exact source sequence as evidence: foreman gathers the crew, identifies edge hazard, checks harness components, orders tie-off before roof access, asks for approved anchor, stops access if no anchor is visible, adds hard hat, and takes a thumbs-up. The source's isolated lanyard-length rule is incomplete for a personal fall-arrest system; OSHA guidance includes free-fall distance, deceleration, harness shift, worker height and safety margin in fall clearance. A harness alone and a thumbs-up do not establish a safe system or verified connection. All 14 card and nine Reader Japanese candidates remain unselected. Qualified roofing safety, Japanese and dictionary review must resolve a source correction before a learner-facing instruction or audio script is authored. Current curriculum has no authored verb-example list; archived forms and six mode labels remain conditional evidence. No progress identity is created.

cards.reviewNote: The source says harness, while archived フルハーネス narrows it to a full-body model. Confirm the intended personal fall-arrest equipment and dictionary sense before selecting a face.
Tie-off / anclarse is the act of connecting to an approved anchorage; archived 墜落防止用の接続 is a description, not necessarily the trade command. Qualified Japanese and fall-protection review required.
Roof anchor / anclaje de techo names an approved attachment point in this scene. Archived 屋根のアンカー may imply any roof-mounted point; do not treat a visible point as approved.
Lanyard / eslinga also has Spanish note cuerda de seguridad. Confirm archived ランヤード identifies the correct connector for the actual system; keep the note distinct from an interchangeable rope claim.
Fall protection is a system-level term; archived 墜落防止 may imply prevention only. Distinguish prevention, restraint and arrest in the dictionary sense.

cards.sourceSpanish: Anclen el arnés antes de subir al techo.
cards.sourceEnglish: Tie off before you go on the roof.
cards.archivedJapanese: 屋根に上がる前にハーネスをアンカーに接続してください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Tie off before you go on the roof.
cards.reviewNote: The isolated command says tie off before roof access, but gives no approved anchor, method or access-point arrangement. Preserve the source without treating the archived Japanese as a complete safe-work instruction.

cards.sourceSpanish: Usen el ancla de techo — nada de improvisar.
cards.sourceEnglish: Use the roof anchor — don't freelance.
cards.archivedJapanese: 屋根のアンカーを使ってください。自己判断で別の場所に接続しないでください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Use the roof anchor — don't freelance.
cards.reviewNote: Use the roof anchor — don't freelance does not identify who approved the anchor or which connection is permitted. Archived 自己判断で別の場所に接続しないでください is plausible but remains an unreviewed safety command.

cards.sourceSpanish: La cuerda de vida corta — que no toquen el suelo si caen.
cards.sourceEnglish: Lanyard short enough you won't hit the ground.
cards.archivedJapanese: 地面に接触しない長さのランヤードを使ってください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Lanyard short enough you won't hit the ground.
cards.reviewNote: The isolated lanyard-short-enough sentence is unsafe as a complete fall-clearance rule: system clearance depends on more than lanyard length. Hold source correction and all Japanese selection pending qualified fall-protection review.

cards.archivedJapanese: 承認されたアンカーを見せてください。
cards.reviewNote: Show me the approved anchor requires prior approval and a clear identification procedure. Archived 承認されたアンカー is unreviewed.

cards.sourceSpanish: Revisen su arnés antes de subir.
cards.sourceEnglish: Check your harness before you climb.
cards.archivedJapanese: 上がる前にハーネスを確認してください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Check your harness before you climb.
cards.reviewNote: Check your harness before climbing omits inspection criteria and the full system. Hold as a source-attributed line, not an approved checklist.

cards.sourceEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness.
cards.archivedJapanese: ハーネスなしでは誰も上がらないでください。
cards.archivedEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness.
cards.reviewNote: Nobody goes up without a harness could wrongly imply a harness alone is sufficient. Hold until the source describes a correctly connected fall-protection system and site-specific controls.

reader.sourceSpanish: Antes de subir, el capataz reúne a la cuadrilla junto a la escalera.
reader.sourceEnglish: Before going up, the foreman gathers the crew next to the ladder.
reader.archivedJapanese: 屋根に上がる前に、職長ははしごの横に作業班を集めます。
reader.archivedEnglish: Before going up, the foreman gathers the crew next to the ladder.

reader.sourceSpanish: Nadie sube sin arnés, porque en el borde del techo hay riesgo de caída.
reader.sourceEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness, because there is a fall hazard at the edge of the roof.
reader.archivedJapanese: 屋根の端には墜落の危険があるため、ハーネスなしでは誰も上がらないでください。
reader.archivedEnglish: Nobody goes up without a harness, because there is a fall hazard at the edge of the roof.
reader.reviewNote: Nobody goes up without a harness may imply the harness alone controls the edge hazard; preserve source and hold an unqualified safety instruction.

reader.sourceSpanish: Revisen su arnés antes de subir: la hebilla, la eslinga y las correas.
reader.sourceEnglish: Check your harness before you climb: the buckle, the lanyard, and the straps.
reader.archivedJapanese: 上がる前に、バックル、ランヤード、ストラップを確認してください。
reader.archivedEnglish: Check your harness before you climb: the buckle, the lanyard, and the straps.
reader.reviewNote: Buckle, lanyard and straps are only a partial inspection list; the line does not establish equipment condition or an approved system.

reader.sourceSpanish: Anclen el arnés antes de subir al techo.
reader.sourceEnglish: Tie your harness off before you go up on the roof.
reader.archivedJapanese: 屋根に上がる前にハーネスをアンカーに接続してください。
reader.archivedEnglish: Tie your harness off before you go up on the roof.
reader.reviewNote: Tie off before roof access lacks the access-point, approved anchorage and connection procedure; do not turn it into a self-contained method.

reader.archivedJapanese: 承認されたアンカーを見せてください。
reader.reviewNote: Show me the approved anchor requires a prior competent approval decision; a visible anchor is not automatically approved.

reader.sourceSpanish: Si no ven un anclaje de techo, no suban y avísenme.
reader.sourceEnglish: If you don't see a roof anchor, don't go up and tell me.
reader.archivedJapanese: 屋根のアンカーが見つからなければ、上がらずに職長に伝えてください。
reader.archivedEnglish: If you don't see a roof anchor, don't go up and tell me.
reader.reviewNote: The stop-and-report instruction if no anchor is visible is useful source language but may not identify the approved access/anchor plan. Preserve the exact line, pending trade review.

reader.sourceEnglish: Put on your hard hat too.
reader.archivedJapanese: ヘルメットも着用してください。
reader.archivedEnglish: Put on your hard hat too.

reader.sourceSpanish: La protección contra caídas solo sirve si cada persona la usa bien.
reader.sourceEnglish: Fall protection only works if each person uses it correctly.
reader.archivedJapanese: 墜落防止は、各自が正しく使って初めて機能します。
reader.archivedEnglish: Fall protection only works if each person uses it correctly.
reader.reviewNote: Fall protection only works if used correctly is broad; distinguish the approved system and required inspection, clearance and rescue plan before learner promotion.

reader.sourceSpanish: Después de anclarse, cada persona levanta el pulgar para avisar al capataz.
reader.sourceEnglish: After tying off, each person gives a thumbs up to let the foreman know.
reader.archivedJapanese: 接続した後、各自が職長に親指を立てて合図します。
reader.archivedEnglish: After tying off, each person gives a thumbs up to let the foreman know.
reader.reviewNote: A thumbs-up after tying off is not a documented verification of the connection or system. Hold the source's implied sufficiency for qualified safety review.

recall.label: Recall tie-off, roof anchor, and fall hazard.

hear.label: Distinguish アンカー from ランヤード when spoken.

type.label: Type 'Check your harness before you climb' in Japanese.

say.label: Give a clear tie-off instruction before roof access.

write.label: Write what the crew checks and shows before going up.
